blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The latest oil price rollback does not make up for losses incurred by fisherfolk after weeks of successive price increases, according to activist fishers’ group Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas (Pamalakaya). In a statement Tuesday, Sept. 29, Pamalakaya said fuel expenses had risen by more than P180 per fishing trip from Sept. 8 to 28, or about P900 for five fishing trips a week. Oil companies began implementing another round of price cuts Tuesday, with diesel prices reduced by more than P7 per liter, according to fuel price advisories. READ: OIL PRICE WATCH as of Sept.
